name: Frozen Shoulder Protocol (Mild)
description: Evidence-based 4-phase program for frozen shoulder. From gentle mobilization through intensive stretching and capsule mobilization to strengthening and return to daily life and sport. Adapted to the clinical stage (freezing/frozen/thawing).
pain_rule: Max. 3/10 pain during exercise. A mild pulling sensation during stretches is acceptable. Sharp or increasing pain requires a break or modification.
evidence_base: Kelley et al. (2009): Frozen shoulder: evidence and a proposed model guiding rehabilitation. JOSPT
Diercks & Stevens (2004): Gentle thawing of the frozen shoulder. Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
Page et al. (2014): Manual therapy and exercise for adhesive capsulitis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
progression_criteria: Pain level acceptable (max. 3/10 during exercise, resolves within 24h)
Range of motion has improved compared to the previous week
Sets/reps completed in 2 consecutive training sessions
No increase in night pain or resting pain

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Pain Management & Gentle Mobilization (Week 0-6)**

In this phase, the focus is on pain relief and maintaining passive range of motion. Gentle pendulum exercises, passive stretches, and isometric strengthening form the foundation.

**Goal:** Reduce pain and maintain passive range of motion.

**Strategy:**
- Pendulum exercises for pain-free mobilization (3-4x daily)
- Passive and active-assisted range of motion in all directions
- Table slides and wall climbing for active-assisted mobilization
- Isometric internal and external rotation for muscle activation
- Thoracic spine mobilization for upright posture

**Scientific basis:** Gentle, pain-adapted mobilization in the early phase is more effective than aggressive stretching and prevents further capsular stiffening (Diercks & Stevens 2004).
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Intensive Stretching & Capsule Mobilization (Week 6-12)**

Acute pain is subsiding. Now we begin with more intensive stretching of the joint capsule and restoration of active range of motion.

**Goal:** Capsule mobilization, expand range of motion.

**Strategy:**
- Active-assisted range of motion with full range
- Specific capsule stretches (cross-body, sleeper stretch)
- Overhead and internal rotation stretching
- Doorframe stretch for anterior capsule and pectoralis
- End-range hold exercises for capsule plasticity

**Scientific basis:** Targeted capsule stretches and end-range mobilization significantly accelerate the restoration of range of motion in adhesive capsulitis (Page et al. 2014).
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Strengthening & Active ROM (Week 12-20)**

Your mobility is returning. Now we build strength and integrate functional movement patterns.

**Goal:** Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises.

**Strategy:**
- Isotonic rotator cuff strengthening with band
- Scapular stabilization exercises (rowing, Y-raises, push-up plus)
- Wall slides with resistance
- Functional overhead reaching for daily life transfer
- Prone T/Y raises for scapular control

**Scientific basis:** Progressive strengthening of the rotator cuff and scapular stabilizers in the thawing phase is crucial for functional recovery (Kelley et al. 2009).
phase_education.4:
**Phase 4: Return & Maintenance (Week 20+)**

You're almost there! In this phase, you return to sport- and work-specific activities and build a maintenance program.

**Goal:** Sport-/work-specific function, long-term maintenance.

**Strategy:**
- Maintenance program for rotator cuff and scapula (2x/week)
- Daily stretching routine (5 minutes)
- Functional overhead training
- Sport-specific drills
- Thoracic spine mobilization as maintenance

**Scientific basis:** A long-term maintenance program reduces the risk of recurrence and secures the regained range of motion in the long run.

exercises.name: Pendulum Exercises (Codman)
exercises.description: Lean your upper body slightly forward, let the arm hang loosely. Let the arm swing in small circles — through weight shifting, not muscle force. 2-3 minutes per round, 3-4x daily.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Passive Flexion (Supine, Stick-Assisted)
exercises.description: Lying on your back, slowly guide the affected arm overhead using a stick or the healthy arm. Only move within the pain-free range.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Passive Abduction (Supine, Stick-Assisted)
exercises.description: Lying on your back, guide the affected arm sideways away from the body using a stick. Slow and controlled to the pain-free limit.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Passive External Rotation (Supine, Stick-Assisted)
exercises.description: Lying on your back, elbow at your side bent at 90 degrees. Slowly rotate the forearm outward using a stick. Keep the shoulder blade stable.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Passive Internal Rotation (Towel Behind Back)
exercises.description: Standing, hold a towel behind your back — healthy hand on top, affected hand on the bottom. The healthy hand gently pulls upward to improve internal rotation. Only go to the pain-free limit.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Table Slides (Flexion & Abduction)
exercises.description: Seated at a table, place your hand on a towel. Slowly slide the arm forward (flexion) and to the side (abduction). The table supports the weight of the arm.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Finger Wall Climbing (Frontal & Lateral)
exercises.description: Stand facing a wall, fingertips on the wall. Slowly 'climb' your fingers upward — frontally and laterally. Mark the highest point and try to reach a little further each day.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Isometric External Rotation
exercises.description: Standing, elbow at your side bent at 90 degrees. Press outward against a wall or door frame. Hold pain-free, then slowly release.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Isometric Internal Rotation
exercises.description: Standing, elbow at your side bent at 90 degrees. Press inward against a wall or door frame. Hold pain-free, then slowly release.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Mobilization (Extension & Rotation)
exercises.description: On all fours or seated: slowly extend and rotate the thoracic spine. Place one hand behind your head and rotate the elbow toward the ceiling. Controlled and without momentum.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief, restore passive range of motion

exercises.name: Active-Assisted Flexion (Full Range)
exercises.description: Supine or standing: guide the affected arm overhead with stick support, then increasingly work actively. Gradually expand range of motion.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Active-Assisted Abduction (Full Range)
exercises.description: Standing or supine: raise the arm sideways with stick support, then increasingly active. Allow the shoulder blade to move in a controlled manner.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Cross-Body Adduction Stretch (Posterior Capsule)
exercises.description: Bring the affected arm across the body at shoulder height. Gently pull it toward the body with the healthy arm. Hold for 30 seconds. Feel the stretch in the back of the shoulder.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch (Posterior Capsule)
exercises.description: Side-lying on the affected side, arm raised to 90 degrees, elbow bent at 90 degrees. Gently press the forearm toward the floor with the free hand. Hold for 30 seconds.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Overhead Towel Stretch
exercises.description: Hold a towel overhead with both hands. Gently pull the affected arm toward overhead extension with the healthy arm. Hold at the end point for 30 seconds.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Doorframe Stretch (Pectoralis & Anterior Capsule)
exercises.description: Stand in a doorframe, forearm on the frame at 90 degrees abduction and 90 degrees elbow flexion. Slowly lean your body forward until you feel a stretch in the chest and front of the shoulder. Hold for 30 seconds.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Internal Rotation Stretch (Towel Behind Back, Intensive)
exercises.description: Towel behind your back, healthy hand on top. Pull more firmly upward than in Phase 1. Gradually bring the affected arm higher toward the middle of the shoulder blade. Hold for 30 seconds.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Active ROM Flexion (Gravity-Assisted to Full)
exercises.description: Standing, actively raise the arm forward and overhead. Slow and controlled. Start gravity-assisted (supine), then standing with full range of motion.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Active ROM Abduction (Gravity-Assisted to Full)
exercises.description: Standing, actively raise the arm sideways. Thumb points upward. Allow the shoulder blade to move in a controlled manner, keep the trunk stable.
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Capsule End-Range Hold Exercises
exercises.description: In each direction of movement (flexion, abduction, external/internal rotation), reach the maximum pain-tolerable end range and hold for 45 seconds. The gentle stretch pain should ease during the hold.
exercises.intensity: At end range of motion — tolerable stretch pain
exercises.phase_goal: Intensive stretching, capsule mobilization, expand range of motion

exercises.name: Isotonic External Rotation with Band
exercises.description: Elbow at your side, bent at 90 degrees. Hold a resistance band in front of your abdomen and rotate the forearm outward. Controlled movement, shoulder blade stays stable.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Isotonic Internal Rotation with Band
exercises.description: Elbow at your side, bent at 90 degrees. Resistance band anchored to the side, rotate the forearm toward the abdomen against the resistance. Slow and controlled.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Scaption with Light Weight
exercises.description: Standing, raise the arm in the scapular plane (30 degrees in front of the frontal plane) to shoulder height, thumb pointing up. Lower in a controlled manner.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Rowing for Scapular Stabilization
exercises.description: Resistance band anchored at chest height. Pull both arms back simultaneously, bringing the shoulder blades together. Keep elbows close to the body.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Serratus Push-Up Plus
exercises.description: Push-up position (wall or incline bench). At the top, additionally push the shoulder blades forward (protraction). Return in a controlled manner.
exercises.intensity: Bodyweight — wall/incline bench/floor depending on level
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Lower Trapezius Y-Raises
exercises.description: Prone position. Raise arms in a Y-position (approx. 135 degrees) off the floor. Thumbs point toward the ceiling. Actively pull shoulder blades down and back.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Wall Slides with Resistance
exercises.description: Back against the wall, forearms on the wall. Slowly slide the arms upward and back. Light band around the wrists for scapular activation.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Active Overhead Reaching (Functional)
exercises.description: Reach for and replace objects at various heights. Simulating daily movements like stocking shelves. Full range of motion, controlled.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Prone T/Y Raises
exercises.description: Prone position. Alternately raise arms in a T-shape (sideways) and Y-shape (diagonally upward) off the floor. Thumbs point upward. Actively squeeze shoulder blades together.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength, active mobility, functional exercises

exercises.name: Rotator Cuff & Scapula Maintenance
exercises.description: Combination of external rotation, rowing, and Y-raises as a maintenance program. 3 exercises in rotation with resistance band or dumbbells. Continue long-term 2x per week.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific function, long-term maintenance

exercises.name: Daily Stretching Routine
exercises.description: Daily stretching program: cross-body stretch, sleeper stretch, doorframe stretch, towel internal rotation, thoracic spine mobilization. Hold each for 30 seconds, 3 repetitions. 5 minutes daily.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific function, long-term maintenance

exercises.name: Functional Overhead Training
exercises.description: Lift, carry, and set down objects overhead. Functional daily loading with progressive weight. Focus on technique and shoulder stability.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific function, long-term maintenance

exercises.name: Sport-Specific Drills
exercises.description: Simulate sport-specific movements (e.g., swimming, tennis, throwing). Start with light resistance, progressively increase. Focus on correct mechanics.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific function, long-term maintenance

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Mobilization (Maintenance)
exercises.description: Thoracic spine mobilization as maintenance program. Extension and rotation seated or on all fours. Prevents renewed stiffness.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific function, long-term maintenance
